objective: Provide an un-biased, falsifiable comparative framework pairing Soviet and Western mathematical literature across identical chronological slices, domains, and ontology schemas.

matching_protocol.schema_uniformity: Western records must be extracted into identical JSONL entity/edge types using the same 17 normalized verbs, operator mappings, and equation family hierarchies.
matching_protocol.citation_density_normalization: Because Western post-war literature has higher total citation counts, comparison metrics are normalized per 1,000 relation edges and evaluated via conditional entropy rather than raw counts.

matched_field_pairs.mathematical_focus: Nonlinear stability of motion, structural robustness, and optimal actuator trajectories.

Pontryagin, Boltyanskii, Gamkrelidze, Mishchenko (1960) Mathematical Theory of Optimal Processes
Krasovskii (1959) Some Problems in the Theory of Stability of Motion
soviet_key_equations: Lyapunov general differential system dx_k/dt = X_k

Pontryagin Maximum Principle condition max_u H
western_landmark_publications: Kalman (1960) A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems
Kalman (1960) Contributions to the Theory of Optimal Control
LaSalle (1960) Some Extensions of Liapunov's Second Method
western_key_equations: Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDE partial V / partial t + min_u [...] = 0
Riccati algebraic differential equation for Kalman gain
matched_field_pairs.expected_relational_contrast: Soviet emphasis traces continuous geometric vector-field perturbation into boundary maximum conditions; Western counterpart emphasizes discrete dynamic programming stages and stochastic variance minimization.

matched_field_pairs.mathematical_focus: Stable reconstruction of internal parameters and sources from incomplete indirect boundary data.

matched_field_pairs.expected_relational_contrast: Soviet framework operationalizes ill-posedness via compact a priori constraint classes and stable regularization operators; Western framework historically categorized ill-posed problems as physically non-meaningful until post-1960 numerical inversion.

matched_field_pairs.expected_relational_contrast: Soviet kinetic tradition treats the self-consistent field as primary and collective oscillations as intrinsic non-local modes; Western tradition initially attempted collisional Boltzmann expansions before adopting BGK nonlinear trapping states.

formal_hypotheses.title: Grammatical Transition Predictability Differential
formal_hypotheses.description: The conditional Shannon entropy of relational transitions between normalized operators and edge types is strictly lower in the Soviet corpus than in the matched Western corpus. This reflects a more constrained, tightly codified sequence of mathematical operations across independent Soviet research schools.
formal_hypotheses.falsification_condition: Delta_H >= 0 (no significant entropy reduction in Soviet transitions).

formal_hypotheses.title: Multi-Resolution Episode Density for Target Grammars
formal_hypotheses.description: The density of multi-resolution episodes corresponding to S1 (Observe->Invert->Constrain->Stabilize), S2 (Represent->Perturb->Stabilize->Control), and S3 (Represent->Reduce->Evolve->Reconstruct) measured across unique equation families and source publications is significantly higher in the Soviet corpus.
formal_hypotheses.falsification_condition: Episode_Ratio(S_i) <= 1.5 across all three target grammars.

formal_hypotheses.title: Relational Verb Vocabulary Divergence
formal_hypotheses.description: The marginal distribution of normalized relation verbs exhibits distinct operational priorities: Soviet mathematics exhibits statistically significant enrichment in STABILIZE, CONSTRAIN, INVERT, and RECONSTRUCT, while Western mathematics exhibits higher relative density in MAP and unconstrained INFER.
formal_hypotheses.test_statistic: Kullback-Leibler divergence D_KL(P_sov || P_west) and verb-by-verb odds ratios
formal_hypotheses.falsification_condition: D_KL < 0.15 bits or failure of STABILIZE/CONSTRAIN enrichment.

verdict_criteria.STRONG_CONFIRMATION: All three hypotheses (H1, H2, H3) confirmed at p < 0.01.
verdict_criteria.MODERATE_CONFIRMATION: H1 confirmed (entropy reduction) and H2 confirmed on at least 2/3 target grammars.
verdict_criteria.FALSIFICATION: H1 fails (Delta_H >= 0), indicating relational transitions are universal to applied mathematics rather than culturally or epistemically distinct.
